composition: Local integration branch based on PR50 with PR51 combined; only package.json and package-lock.json conflicted. Dependency maps were united at their exact existing versions and lockfile regenerated with Node22. No remote PR merge or deployment.
e2e: npm run test:pilot, explicit RUN_PILOT_E2E=1, loopback mblz_ci only. Real Next server, real database services and Chromium UI. Two synthetic verified accounts seeded through real registration service with fake in-memory mail; SMTP configuration forcibly empty in child server. AUTH_LOCAL_ENABLED=true only in isolated child process. Exercises password login, workspace UI, saved/reloaded model, field filling, review, v2 save/reopen, approval locks/unlocks, second-tab v3, reopen/approve expectedVersion3 with zero409, actual DOCX/PDF downloads, second-account denial, logout/relogin/reopen. Evidence is retained as CI artifact; no password/token trace is captured.
P2_regression: The original 8f870602 editor failed APPROVED-to-DRAFT refresh in local Chromium. Fixed by PR49 HEAD80f81b1: serverVersion/serverStatus effect dependencies and router refresh on manual reopen. Both component regression and authenticated integration tests assert this behavior.
placeholders: Text-only LawyerMind identity; screenshots annotated as synthetic and without approved logo or VCL letterhead. Export UI explicitly says sem timbrado. Supplied logo and timbrado are not delivered.
production_preflight_plan: Obtain separate authorization and a named operator, maintenance window and verified backup/PITR restore point. Do not configure secrets or enable auth during code review.

Only after authorization, run scripts/preflight/local-auth-readonly.sql with a read-only role against the selected database. Inspect duplicate normalized-email group counts and existing schema; output contains group fingerprints rather than raw email addresses. This task has NOT executed it against production.

Any duplicate lower(btrim(email)), unexpected existing objects or schema drift blocks migration. A human must separately assess account ownership; never auto-merge users, normalize existing emails, activate legacy passwords or delete records.

Rehearse migration and restore on a separately authorized sanitized staging clone. Confirm Google login, flag-off paths, registration denial for existing users, session revocation and index behavior. Capture exact migration/schema revision.

Keep AUTH_LOCAL_ENABLED=false. Apply additive migration in a separately approved operation using npm run db:deploy, with snapshot/restore readiness and lock/statement timeout appropriate to measured table size. Do not run it implicitly during application start: start script now only invokes next start.

Enable only after separately approved SMTP secret configuration, canonical HTTPS origin, retry scheduler and staging delivery checks. No new credentials, scheduler or production changes were made here.
rollback_plan: Disable AUTH_LOCAL_ENABLED to stop password authentication and queue processing; this is a planned emergency configuration action, not performed here. Existing Google authentication remains available; local-only users will temporarily lose access, so communicate via an approved operator channel.

Stop delivery retries and revert application release if necessary. Preserve additive auth tables, local users, sessions/audit evidence and unique index; do not use destructive down-migrations or automatically reconcile accounts.

If migration fails before activation, keep auth off and capture Prisma migration state. Do not issue migrate resolve or rerun partially applied SQL blindly; compare each created object against the approved migration and restore from the tested backup or perform a separately reviewed recovery.
Any later index removal/table deletion/data restoration requires its own reviewed plan and approval, including consistency of users created after deployment.
local_limit: Prisma checksum download returned HTTP403; no ignore-checksum or alternative-download bypass. Full generated-client/database/E2E validation is performed in disposable CI where official install succeeds.
